title: French diocesan missals, batch 4 (lane B): original-book and scholarly-described book states

traditions.label: Toulouse diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Printed missals of the metropolitan church of Saint-Étienne, Toulouse, as attested by two directly inspected originals (1490 and 1774).
traditions.coverage_note: Two publication states are documented from original leaves. The 1501–1552 prints, the 1773/1774 catalogue pair, the 1832 missal and the date of adoption of the Roman Missal remain open; no component collation links the two states.

traditions.label: Soissons diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Soissons diocesan Mass books: the 1687 Roman Missal with Soissons proper and the 1745 Fitz-James missal.
traditions.coverage_note: A 1687 Roman-Missal-plus-proper state (description) and the 1745 Fitz-James missal (original) are documented. The 1516/1531 prints, the post-Tridentine Soissons missal and the 1852 Roman restoration act remain open.

traditions.label: Vienne diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Printed missals of the church and province of Vienne: a Lyon-printed missal of 1519/1520 (inspected original) and the 1782 provincial missal (described).
traditions.coverage_note: A 1519/1520 publication state (original) and the 1782 promulgation of the provincial missal (scholarly description) are documented. Inspected copies of the provincial missal, its reprints and the Roman restorations remain open.

traditions.label: Nantes diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Printed Nantes missals described at exact loci in Duine's 1906 bibliography of Breton liturgical books.
traditions.coverage_note: Two sixteenth-century publication states are documented from scholarly description; the 1482 print, the eighteenth-century Poitiers-type liturgy, the 1837 missal and the 1858 Roman adoption remain without inspected book evidence.

traditions.label: Rennes diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Printed Rennes missals described at exact loci in Duine 1906.
traditions.coverage_note: Four fifteenth/sixteenth-century publication states are documented from scholarly description. The eighteenth-century missals, the 1780 cathedral-only adoption of the Tours liturgy and the Roman adoption (1846 or 1848) remain unverified against books.

traditions.label: Vannes diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Printed Vannes missals of 1530 and 1535 as reported by Duine 1906.
traditions.coverage_note: Only a provisional 1535 state rests on a scholarly report with second-hand contents; no documented state.

traditions.label: Léon (Saint-Pol-de-Léon) diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The 1526 Missale Leonense as described by Duine 1906.
traditions.coverage_note: One publication state is documented from scholarly description; later Léon books and the see's suppression in 1790/1801 are outside the evidence.

traditions.label: Sées diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Sées diocesan Mass book from the 1742 Néel de Christot missal, as stated by diocesan historians.
traditions.coverage_note: One eighteenth-century publication state is documented from scholarship. The medieval prints, the earlier adoption of Roman books, the 1841 missal and the 1864 Roman ordinance are recorded as gaps.

traditions.label: Thérouanne (Morinensis) diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Printed missals for the use of Thérouanne before the see's destruction in 1553 and partition in 1559.
traditions.coverage_note: Two publication states are documented from a descriptive bibliography. The route has a historical endpoint: the see was suppressed after 1553 and partitioned on 29 June 1559.

stages.label: 1490 Toulouse missal (Kleblat)
stages.date_label: Printed Toulouse, colophon and prefatory letter both dated 24 July 1490
stages.scope: One identified 1490 printing, its prefatory chapter letter, colophon and a calendar leaf.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum sancti Stephani Tolosae, Toulouse 1490, BM Toulouse Inc. Toulouse 106
stages.summary: A printed letter in the name of Archbishop Pierre de Lion, the provost Pierre de Rosergio and the chapter says that solemn Masses were celebrated with much discord because manuscript missals were old, faulty or disordered. They therefore had a missal ordered according to the church's rite, corrected by a named canon, and printed by Stephanus Kleblat for distribution throughout the archdiocese, exhorting deans, priors, archpriests and rectors to provide copies and celebrate according to it. The colophon names the book as for the metropolitan church of Saint-Étienne and dates it 24 July 1490. The November calendar carries Toulouse saints: Papulus (3 November) and Saturninus as a double (29 November), the latter line ending with 'Vigilia', the vigil of St Andrew.

evidence.locus: Canvas 7, unnumbered preliminary leaf recto, letter 'Universis…'
evidence.claim: Archbishop, provost and chapter order a corrected missal according to the Toulouse rite, printed by Kleblat and commended to the clergy of the diocese; dated 24 July 1490.

evidence.locus: Canvas 613, provider label XVIIv, right column
evidence.claim: Colophon: book of the missal for the metropolitan church of Saint-Étienne, printed by Stephanus Kleblat, 24 July 1490; printer's mark; preceded by the Prosa pro mortuis.
Calendar includes Papulus (3 November) and Saturninus, double (29 November), followed on the same line by 'Vigilia' (the vigil of Andrew, 30 November).

stages.limitations: No prayer, Ordo or Canon text was read. The letter states a corrective purpose; it does not identify an exemplar or describe specific textual changes. Earlier manuscript Toulouse missals remain uncompared.
stages.reception: The letter exhorts the diocesan clergy to obtain and use the printed missal; it is an exhortation, and actual adoption is not established.

stages.label: 1774 Toulouse missal (Loménie de Brienne)
stages.date_label: Title dated 1774; archbishop's pastoral letter dated 29 October 1772 (4 Kal. Nov.)
stages.scope: One identified 1774 printing, its title and the archbishop's complete pastoral letter describing the edition's programme.
stages.witness_label: Missale Tolosanum, Toulouse 1774, Google Books rZCkXZ7X0VQC
stages.summary: The title names Archbishop Étienne-Charles de Loménie de Brienne's authority with chapter consent. His letter says the new missal was made to agree with his recently published breviary (same Gospels, collects and scriptural chant texts) while keeping the Latin rite and order. It describes the distribution of Gospel and Epistle readings, with at least three ferial Gospels each week (Monday, Wednesday and Friday), each paired with its own Epistle. It says that the old Toulouse missal already gave proper Gospels to Advent ferias except Saturday. Chant texts were largely adopted from French missals, especially the Paris missal. Most orations came from the ancient sacramentaries. Prefaces were added for Advent, Septuagesima, saints, Corpus Christi, the Dedication and Toulouse saints, with two prefaces for Stephen and Saturninus taken from the old Missale Gothicum. Old sequences were kept for Easter, Pentecost, Christmas and Corpus Christi, and the rest came from the Paris missal. A Mass for the King was added. The letter commands all churches, chapters, monasteries, convents, seminaries, colleges, communities, orders and priests bound to the Toulouse Office to use this missal and forbids others.

evidence.claim: Missale Tolosanum by Loménie de Brienne's authority with chapter consent; Toulouse, Bibliopolae Usuum Tolosanorum, 1774, with royal privilege.
Primary description of the edition's programme: conformity to the new breviary, Gospel/Epistle distribution, sources of chants, orations, prefaces and sequences, Missa pro Rege.

evidence.locus: PA8–PA9, letter printed pp. 8–9; RA1-PP14 Monitum
evidence.claim: Mandate with addressees and prohibition of other missals; dateline 4 Kal. Nov. 1772, signed and countersigned; Monitum lists marginal source sigla (Roman and Gallican sacramentaries, Ambrosian, Paris 1685/1705/1738, old Toulouse, new Reims, Lyon missals).

stages.limitations: The letter's account of change is a contemporary claim; no predecessor missal was collated. The 1772 letter date and the 1774 title date are distinct events. Whether this copy belongs to the same printing as the catalogue's 1773 entry is unresolved.
stages.reception: The letter commands all churches, chapters, monasteries, convents, seminaries, colleges, communities and orders of the diocese, and priests bound by law or custom to the Toulouse Office, to use this missal and forbids others. The printed command names its addressees; it does not establish uniform actual uptake, a first effective-use date or the duration of use.

stages.label: 1687 Roman Missal with Proprium Missalis Suessionensis
stages.date_label: Proper printed at Soissons (Hanisset), cum permissu, 1687 (as described)
stages.scope: A Roman-Missal state: a Roman Missal with a printed Soissons proper bound after it, as described by Leclercq de Laprairie.
stages.witness_label: Missale Romanum with Proprium Missalis Suessionensis, Soissons 1687 (Acy church and seminary copies)
stages.summary: Leclercq de Laprairie describes a Roman Missal at the church of Acy followed by a 'Proprium Missalis Suessionensis' printed at Soissons by Hanisset with permission in 1687, during a vacancy of the see; the seminary library had another copy. He says the liturgy given by Bishop de Bourlon was that prescribed by Pius V, keeping many local elements. Ledouble confirms that the missal appeared after Bourlon's death, in 1687.

evidence.claim: Roman Missal with Proprium Missalis Suessionensis, Soissons, Hanisset, 1687; Bourlon's liturgy that of Pius V with retained local elements.
The missal of Bourlon's liturgy appeared in 1687, after his death.

stages.limitations: Copies described, not viewed; the edition of the Roman Missal is not identified. The 1745 letter's report of churches forced to use the Roman Missal is consistent with this state but is a separate statement.
stages.reception: The described copies belonged to a parish church and the seminary; diocesan uptake is not established.

stages.label: 1745 Soissons missal (Fitz-James)
stages.date_label: Title dated 1745; episcopal letter dated Soissons, 6 January 1745
stages.scope: One identified 1745 printing, its title and the bishop's complete letter describing the edition.
stages.witness_label: Missale Suessionense, Paris 1745, BM Lyon SJ LB 030/68 (Numelyo; Google Books JWXbxJ1ccrQC)
stages.summary: Bishop François de Fitz-James issues the missal after his new breviary. He says that copies of the Soissons missal hardly survived, so almost all churches had been forced to use the Roman Missal, and that Soissons rites survived only orally and were mixed with Roman ones. Apart from the orations, the body of the missal is composed from Scripture. Proper Epistles and Gospels for Wednesdays and Fridays are presented as an old Soissons usage, found in older Soissons missals including one printed shortly after Trent. The Gospels are distributed so that all four evangelists are read in a year. Orations come mostly from ancient sacramentaries, and a few prefaces were added (for example Advent and principal feasts). Lapsed rites common to neighbouring churches of the Reims province were restored, following Sixtus V's principle. All churches, chapters, pastors, monasteries, colleges, communities, sodalities and priests bound to the Soissons Office must use this missal; other missals and rites are forbidden.

evidence.claim: Missale Suessionense by Fitz-James's authority with chapter consent; Paris, J.-B. Coignard, 1745, royal privilege.
Primary description: prior forced use of the Roman Missal for want of Soissons copies; scriptural composition; Wednesday/Friday lessons; sacramentary orations; added prefaces; restored rites.
Mandate to the named institutions and priests; prohibition of other missals and rites; dated Soissons, 6 January 1745.

stages.limitations: The letter's comparison with earlier practice is a contemporary claim; no earlier Soissons missal or Roman Missal was collated. The post-Tridentine Soissons edition it mentions is unidentified.
stages.reception: The letter commands all churches, chapters, pastors, monasteries, colleges, communities, sodalities and priests bound to the Soissons Office. The printed command names its addressees; it does not establish uniform actual uptake, a first effective-use date or the duration of use.

stages.label: 1782 Vienne provincial missal (Lefranc de Pompignan)
stages.date_label: Pastoral letter dated 18 August 1782 promulgating the missal and breviary; publication reported as 1783; catalogue year 1784
stages.scope: The promulgation of a common missal and breviary for the province of Vienne, as described from the pastoral letter by the 1849 survey and by Pompignan's biographer.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum provinciae Viennensis (catalogue year 1784)
stages.summary: The 1849 survey describes Archbishop Lefranc de Pompignan's pastoral letter of 18 August 1782. It is addressed to the clergy of Vienne and, with the comprovincial bishops' consent, to the clergy of each diocese of the province, and it promulgates the new missal and breviary together. The author says Pompignan replaced the earlier Villars liturgy by adopting the Paris books of Vintimille, Viger and Mésenguy with some cuts, additions and corrections, after the provincial assembly of 1775. Pompignan's 1903 biographer notes that the breviary and missal were published in 1783 at Grenoble by the widow Giroud, with a Latin preface on the wish for books common to the province.

evidence.claim: Pastoral letter of 18 August 1782 promulgating the provincial missal and breviary; Paris-model books with corrections; 1775 provincial assembly.
Breviary and missal published 1783, Grenoble, widow Giroud, with a Latin preface on common provincial books.

stages.limitations: The letter was not viewed; its content is reported by a polemical survey. Publication is reported as 1783, while the catalogue witness is dated 1784; edition identity with the witness is assumed, not verified. The extent of dependence on the Paris missal is the author's judgement, not a collation.
stages.reception: The letter addresses the clergy of the whole province with the suffragans' consent; actual uptake in Grenoble, Valence, Viviers and Die is not established.

stages.label: 1519/1520 Vienne missal (Lescuyer, Lyon)
stages.date_label: Colophon: printed at Lyon, last day of February 1519 (possibly 1520 new style)
stages.scope: One identified Lyon printing for the use of Vienne: title, colophon and a calendar leaf.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum sancte Viennensis ecclesie, Lyon 1519, BM Lyon (Numelyo)
stages.summary: The colophon calls it the missal for the use of the holy church of Vienne, with very many offices newly added, printed at Lyon by Bernard Lescuyer on the last day of February 1519. The February calendar lists the Vienne bishops Avitus (5 February) and Simplicius (11 February), and Paschasius (22 February), with folio references to the sanctoral.

evidence.claim: Red title: missal for the use of the holy church of Vienne; Lyon library stamp.
Missal for the use of Vienne, with offices newly added; printed at Lyon by Bernard Lescuyer, last day of February 1519.
Calendar entries for Avitus and Simplicius, bishops of Vienne, and Paschasius, with sanctoral folio references.

stages.limitations: The phrase 'offices newly added' names no specific Masses, and no earlier Vienne missal was compared. No bishop's mandate was seen. The date bounds cover the year-style uncertainty, not a duration.
stages.reception: The title and colophon designate Vienne use; actual diocesan adoption is not established.

stages.label: 1520 Nantes missal (Rouen, Martin Morin)
stages.date_label: 1520 printing, as described by Duine from BnF Rés. B.1814
stages.scope: One identified 1520 printing (quarto, Rouen, Martin Morin) and one contents observation reported by Duine.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum insignis ecclesie Nannetensis, Rouen 1520 (Duine no. 46; BnF Rés. B.1814)
stages.summary: Duine describes the BnF copy as a quarto printed at Rouen by Martin Morin. At fol. CIII, after the ordinary Gloria, it has the Marian-farced 'Gloria de beata Maria', which Duine notes is not peculiar to Breton use.

evidence.claim: 1520 Nantes missal, Rouen, Martin Morin, BnF Rés. B.1814; second Gloria de beata Maria at fol. CIII.

stages.limitations: Scholarly description only; the original was not viewed. Copy identity with the USUARIUM 1520 record is assumed at edition level, not verified.
stages.reception: The title designates Nantes use; actual adoption is not established.

stages.label: 1588 Nantes missal (Philippe du Bec)
stages.date_label: 1588 printing at Nantes (Vincent Hucet), title transcribed by Duine
stages.scope: One identified 1588 printing whose transcribed title states episcopal mandate and approximation to the Tridentine exemplar.
stages.witness_label: Missale secundum usum insignis ecclesie Nanetensis, Nantes 1588 (Duine no. 47; BM Nantes 1277)
stages.summary: Duine transcribes the title of the Nantes municipal library copy. It was issued by mandate of Bishop Philippe du Bec, as approaching nearest to the Tridentine exemplar ('Ad exemplar Tridentinum proxime accedens'), and recently emended by men delegated in the Nantes synod. It was printed at Nantes by Vincent Hucet with royal privilege in 1588: a folio in roman type, in two columns.

evidence.claim: Title transcription: du Bec mandate, approximation to the Tridentine exemplar, synodal emendation; Nantes, Vincent Hucet, 1588.

stages.limitations: The title's claim of approximation to the Tridentine missal is the book's self-description reported by Duine; the extent of conformity to the 1570 Roman Missal is not collated. Duine's section heading prints the year ambiguously; the transcribed title ends 1588.
stages.reception: The title records episcopal mandate and synodal delegation; actual diocesan uptake is not established.

stages.label: 1492 Rennes missal (Michel Guibé)
stages.date_label: Colophon: finished at Paris, 10 January 1492 (as quoted by Duine); year style not stated, so possibly January 1493 by modern reckoning
stages.scope: One identified printing whose colophon, quoted by Duine, states episcopal correction.
stages.witness_label: Missale ecclesie Redonensis, Paris, colophon 10 January 1492 (Duine no. 10; BnF Vélins 201 = catalogue witness 7428)
stages.summary: Duine quotes the colophon. The missal and ordinary of the Mass, with the church's constitutions and customs added, omissions supplied and errors emended, was prepared by order of Bishop Michel Guibé through four named clergy and printed at Paris at the cost of the booksellers André Hodian and Jean Alexandre. It was finished on 10 January 1492.

evidence.claim: Colophon quoted: correction by order of Bishop Michel Guibé; Paris; finished 10 January 1492.

stages.limitations: Duine does not say whether the January date follows a year beginning at Easter; the bounds 1492–1493 express that year-style uncertainty, not a duration. Original not viewed; the described BnF copy is the holding of catalogue witness 7428, whose own age field is malformed.
stages.reception: The colophon records episcopal commission; actual adoption is not established.

stages.label: 1523 Rennes missal (Yves Mahyeuc)
stages.date_label: 1523 printing at Paris (Jean de Kerbriant), as described by Duine
stages.scope: One identified printing with its title, final-page statement of episcopal correction and approval, and added Masses.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad consuetudinem insignis ecclesie Redonensis, Paris 1523 (Duine no. 12; Arsenal 2742)
stages.summary: Duine quotes the title, which mentions the church's institutions and customs. He reports from the last page that the missal was corrected by order of Bishop Yves Mahyeuc and approved by him. It gained Masses of Our Lady of Pity, St Roch, St Claude and the Holy Name, and was printed at Paris by Jean de Kerbriant, alias Huguelin, in 1523.

evidence.claim: Title; correction by order of and approval by Bishop Yves; added Masses of Our Lady of Pity, Roch, Claude, Holy Name; Paris, Kerbriant, 1523.

stages.limitations: Duine paraphrases the final page; the added Masses are reported, not collated against 1492. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: Episcopal approval is reported; actual uptake is not established.

stages.label: 1531 Rennes missal (Caen)
stages.date_label: Title imprint 1531, printed at Caen (as described by Duine)
stages.scope: One identified printing with its title and Duine's contents remarks on the Order of Mass.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum insignis ecclesie Redonensis, 1531 (Duine no. 13)
stages.summary: The title, as transcribed, says the missal was skilfully emended with several additions and newly joined Masses; Duine lists the Holy Name, Lacryma Christi, Visitation, Roch, Genevieve and Martha. He notes farced Kyries and two Glorias. He also notes that the Mass ends with the Placeat, without a final blessing or last Gospel.

evidence.locus: PA41 and PA43, printed pp. 41, 43, no. 13
evidence.claim: Title with added Masses and 1531 imprint, Caen; contents remarks on Kyries, Glorias and the ending of the Mass.

stages.limitations: No bishop is named. Duine's remark that the Mass ends at the Placeat is his observation of one copy. The 1533 entry may be a second issue of this edition (Duine against Delisle).
stages.reception: Title designates Rennes use; uptake not established.

stages.label: 1588 Rennes missal (Aymar Hennequin)
stages.date_label: 1588 printing at Rennes (Pierre Bretel), title transcribed by Duine
stages.scope: One identified printing whose title states restoration and emendation by episcopal order with chapter consent.
stages.witness_label: Missale insignis ecclesiae Rhedonensis, Rennes 1588 (Duine no. 16)
stages.summary: Duine transcribes the title of the Grand Séminaire copy. It was restored and emended by order of Bishop Aymar Hennequin with the chapter's consent, and printed at Rennes by Pierre Bretel in 1588 with royal privilege. The sequences are gathered at the end, to be said or omitted at the celebrant's choice. The Ordinarium Missae offers an alternative litany-form Kyrie in three forms (fol. 159v–160r).

evidence.claim: Title with Hennequin order and chapter consent, Rennes 1588; sequences gathered at the end as optional; Kyrie alternatives fol. 159v–160r.

stages.limitations: Original not viewed; not among the Amiet-table witnesses. No claim of Roman conformity is made by the transcribed title.
stages.reception: Episcopal order with chapter consent is recorded; uptake not established.

stages.label: 1535 Vannes missal (Paris, Yolande Bonhomme)
stages.date_label: 1535 printing, as reported by Duine
stages.scope: Printing facts and one contents report for the 1535 Vannes missal.
stages.witness_label: Missel vannetais de 1535 (Duine no. 53; Vannes episcopal library)
stages.summary: Duine reports a copy in the Vannes episcopal library, printed at Paris by Yolande Bonhomme, widow of Thielman Kerver, for Nantes and Vannes booksellers. An old manuscript note in the 1589 breviary, which he quotes, says that this missal gave St Denis a sequence and Credo for the whole diocese.

evidence.claim: Printing facts for the 1535 Vannes missal and a quoted manuscript note on its St Denis sequence and Credo.

stages.limitations: Provisional: Duine gives no title, colophon or mandate text, and the contents claim is second-hand through a manuscript note. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1526 Léon missal (Paris, Nicolas Prévost)
stages.date_label: 1526 printing at Paris, per the last leaf as reported by Duine
stages.scope: One identified printing, its last-leaf statement and Order-of-Mass remarks reported by Duine.
stages.witness_label: Missale Leonense, Paris 1526: edition described by Duine no. 63 (he names copies at the BnF, Rés. B.27804, and the Quimper Grand Séminaire); catalogue witness 6499 is the Quimper diocesan-library holding, matched at edition level
stages.summary: Duine reports from the last leaf that the missal was printed in 1526 at Paris by Nicolas Prévost at the cost of Yves Quilleveré. He quotes the phrase 'prefateque ecclesie ritui adaptatum', which he interprets as adapting the Léon liturgy to the Paris liturgy. He notes a Confiteor that does not copy the Roman formula, two different Glorias and farced Kyries.

evidence.claim: Printing facts from the last leaf; quoted adaptation phrase; Confiteor, Gloria and Kyrie remarks.

stages.limitations: The quoted Latin phrase literally refers to the rite of 'the aforesaid church'; Duine's reading of it as Paris use is his interpretation and is not adopted here. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1742 Sées missal (Néel de Christot)
stages.date_label: Missal printed 1742 (Hommey); mandate date not given
stages.scope: The fact, date and episcopal authorship of the 1742 Sées missal, and its stated relation to the diocesan breviaries, as reported by Hommey.
stages.witness_label: Missale Sagiense, 1742 (Néel de Christot)
stages.summary: Hommey says Bishop Néel de Christot completed Jacques Lallemant's liturgy and promulgated its missal and ritual. He adds that the missal, printed in 1742, and Néel de Christot's 1745 breviary did not agree with Lallemant's breviary. Marais and Beaudouin date Lallemant's breviary mandement to 15 August 1737 and say that the Roman breviary had been in use at Sées for over a century before it.

evidence.locus: PA56 and PA409, printed pp. 56 and 409
evidence.claim: Néel de Christot promulgated the missal completing Lallemant's liturgy; missal printed 1742; disagreement with Lallemant's breviary.

evidence.locus: PA217 and PA220, printed pp. 217 and 220
evidence.claim: Lallemant's new breviary promulgated by mandement of 15 August 1737 after more than a century of Roman breviary use.

stages.limitations: No original page or mandate text was viewed; the content of the missal is not described beyond its relation to the breviaries.
stages.reception: Promulgation is stated; actual uptake is not established.

stages.label: 1516 Thérouanne missal (Rouen, Martin Morin)
stages.date_label: Final note: 12 November 1516 (as reported in French by the bibliography)
stages.scope: One identified printing: title, colophon and printer as transcribed in the Saint-Omer bibliography.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum insignis ecclesie Morinensis, Rouen 1516
stages.summary: The bibliography transcribes the title and reports, without transcribing it, the final note. The missal was printed at the cost of Jean and Antoine Lagache, booksellers at Arras, on 12 November 1516, by Martin Morin at Rouen.

evidence.claim: Title transcribed for Thérouanne use; final note reported: Lagache expense; Martin Morin, Rouen; 12 November 1516.

stages.limitations: Publication facts only; no contents described. Component scope is nominal. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: Title designates Thérouanne use; uptake not established.

stages.label: 1518 Thérouanne missal (Paris, Nicolas de Pratis)
stages.date_label: Colophon: Paris, 11 September 1518 (as transcribed)
stages.scope: One identified printing whose transcribed title claims correction, placement of the sequences and added Masses.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum insignis ecclesie Morinensis, Paris 1518
stages.summary: The transcribed title calls the missal well ordered and carefully corrected, with the sequences set in their places and several Masses added that had never before been printed in that use. The colophon reads Paris, Nicolas de Pratis, at the expense of de Pratis and Jean de Laporte, 11 September 1518. A calendar with monthly health advice follows.

evidence.claim: Title claiming correction, placed sequences and added Masses; colophon 11 September 1518; calendar noted.

stages.limitations: The added Masses are not named; no collation with 1516. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: Title designates Thérouanne use; uptake not established.

stages.label: 1497 Troyes missal (Paris, Jean du Pré)
stages.date_label: Colophon dated 17 February 1497 at Paris (as described by Lalore); year style not stated, so possibly February 1498 by modern reckoning
stages.scope: Publication facts of one printing from Lalore's description.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum insignis ecclesie Trecensis, Paris 1497
stages.summary: Lalore describes the 1497 missal printed at Paris by Jean du Pré for the Troyes bookseller Nicolas Ludot, with a colophon calling the book corrected of errors.

evidence.claim: 1497 Troyes missal: colophon, printer and bookseller.

stages.limitations: Publication facts only; component scope nominal. Lalore also lists an earlier 1492 edition, not among the Amiet-table witnesses. Original not viewed. The bounds 1497–1498 express the colophon's year-style uncertainty, not a duration.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1525 Troyes missal (Le Coq)
stages.date_label: Colophon dated 1525 (as described by Lalore)
stages.scope: One printing and its colophon's statement of added Masses.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum insignis ecclesie Trecensis, Troyes 1525
stages.summary: Lalore quotes the colophon of the 1525 Le Coq printing, which reports added Masses of SS Joseph, Godo and Edmund.

evidence.claim: 1525 colophon with added Masses of Joseph, Godo and Edmund.

stages.limitations: Added Masses reported, not collated against 1497. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1580 Troyes missal (Claude de Bauffremont)
stages.date_label: Bishop's mandate dated 1 March 1580; printed 1580
stages.scope: One edition 'recently emended' by episcopal mandate, with Lalore's reprint of the mandate.
stages.witness_label: Missale secundum usum insignis ecclesiae Trecensis, Troyes 1580
stages.summary: Lalore describes the 1580 edition, whose title says it was recently emended by the bishop's mandate. He prints Bishop Claude de Bauffremont's Latin mandate for it, dated at Troyes on 1 March 1580. Lalore reports that the 1615 Troyes missal is a reprint of this edition.

evidence.claim: 1580 edition 'recens emendatum'; Bauffremont's mandate dated 1 March 1580; 1615 reprint.

stages.limitations: The mandate does not claim conformity to the 1570 Roman Missal; no collation. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: The mandate commands the edition; uptake not established.

stages.label: 1696 Roman Missal with Troyes supplement
stages.date_label: Supplement printed 1696; use described in the 1736 mandate
stages.scope: A Roman-Missal state: the Roman Missal used with a printed diocesan supplement of proper prayers.
stages.witness_label: Orationes addendae Missali Romano pro celebrantibus missam ritu dioecesis Trecensis, Troyes 1696
stages.summary: Bossuet's 1736 mandate says that Troyes missals had become so scarce that all churches, including the cathedral, had long used only 'foreign missals', which his predecessors had tolerated. Lalore's footnote identifies these as the Roman Missal with the diocesan supplement printed in 1696 under the title Orationes addendae Missali Romano … ritu dioecesis Trecensis (Troyes, Charles Briden).

evidence.locus: PA83 and PA113, printed pp. 83, 113 with footnote 1
evidence.claim: 1696 supplement to the Roman Missal for the Troyes rite; 1736 mandate on the long use of 'foreign missals'.

stages.limitations: The duration and universality of this use are the 1736 mandate's statement; the supplement's contents are not described beyond its title. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: The 1736 mandate says the cathedral and all churches used these books, with episcopal toleration.

stages.label: 1736 Troyes missal (Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet)
stages.date_label: First mandate 16 September 1735; publication mandate 26 September 1736
stages.scope: The 1736 Bossuet missal, its two mandates and the documented controversy and correction mandate.
stages.witness_label: Missale Trecense, Troyes 1736 (Bossuet)
stages.summary: Lalore prints Bishop Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet's Latin mandate of 16 September 1735 and his French mandate of 26 September 1736. The latter presents the missal as made to answer the new breviary, prepared by learned men chosen with the chapter, and as the awaited replacement for the foreign missals whose use his predecessors had tolerated; Lalore's chronology (p. 111) records it as making the new missal obligatory. Lalore's chronology records a royal commission under Cardinal de Rohan, a Conseil d'État arrêt of 11 June 1737, and Bossuet's fourth pastoral instruction and ordinance of 15 October 1738, in which he retracted several provisions of the missal and restored the former rubrics on three principal points (pp. 112, 117).

evidence.claim: Mandates of 16 September 1735 and 26 September 1736 for the new Troyes missal.
Controversy chronology: Rohan commission, arrêt of 11 June 1737, and the 15 October 1738 instruction and ordinance retracting several provisions and restoring former rubrics on three points.

stages.limitations: The ordered corrections of 1738 imply a corrected state whose printed form was not seen; no collation with the Roman Missal or the 1580 book. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: The 1736 mandate orders use by the diocese; the controversy shows contested reception; uptake not established.

stages.label: 1532 Mâcon missal (Lyon, Denys de Harsy)
stages.date_label: Colophon dated 15 March 1532 (as described)
stages.scope: One printing described with title, colophon and contents divisions.
stages.witness_label: Missale Matisconense, Lyon, Denys de Harsy, 1532
stages.summary: The Notes describe a 1532 Mâcon missal printed at Lyon by Denys de Harsy, with a colophon of 15 March 1532. Its title says it was newly emended and carefully corrected, with several new offices not seen before. The book bears the arms of Bishop Hémard de Denonville and contains Temporale, Sanctorale and Commune.

evidence.claim: 1532 Mâcon missal: title claiming emendation and new offices; Lyon, Harsy, 15 March 1532; arms; divisions.

stages.limitations: New offices are claimed but not named; no collation. Original not viewed; not among the Amiet-table witnesses.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1509 Verdun missal (Paris, Wolfgang Hopyl)
stages.date_label: 1509 printing (as described)
stages.scope: One printing commissioned by the chapter during a vacancy, as described.
stages.witness_label: Missale Virdunense, Paris, Hopyl, 1509
stages.summary: The Petite bibliothèque verdunoise describes the 1509 missal printed on vellum at Paris by Wolfgang Hopyl by order of the chapter while the see was vacant: 284 leaves, the Verdun copy perhaps unique. The Pouillé also records it.

evidence.claim: 1509 Verdun missal: chapter commission sede vacante; Hopyl; vellum; 284 leaves.
1509 missal recorded.

stages.limitations: Publication facts only; no contents. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: Chapter commission recorded; uptake not established.

stages.label: 1554 Verdun missal (Nicolas Psaulme)
stages.date_label: Title year 1554; the Pouillé dates a reprint to 1557
stages.scope: One edition by Bishop Psaulme with title and contents divisions as described.
stages.witness_label: Missale … ecclesie et diocesis Virdunensis, Paris 1554 (Psaulme)
stages.summary: The Petite bibliothèque verdunoise transcribes the title: newly and carefully revised by Bishop Nicolas Psaulme, with many additions never printed before, including several Mass offices, and printed at the bishop's expense in 1554. It describes the divisions: preliminaries, Proper of Time with the Ordo Missae up to the Canon, Canon, Sanctorale, Common and votives. The Pouillé instead says that Psaulme had the Verdun missal reprinted in 1557.

evidence.claim: Psaulme title (revised, many additions), 1554, and contents divisions.
Reprint by Psaulme dated 1557.

stages.limitations: The 1554/1557 discrepancy is unresolved and may reflect two issues. The revision is pre-Tridentine and makes no Roman-conformity claim. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1556 Meaux missal (Louis de Brézé)
stages.date_label: 1556 edition (Allou)
stages.scope: A corrected new edition of the earlier Meaux missal, as recorded.
stages.witness_label: Missale … ecclesie Meldensis, 1556
stages.summary: Allou says that in 1556 Bishop Louis de Brézé gave a new edition of Jean L'Huillier's missal, corrected by his care. Allou dates L'Huillier's printed missal to 1492.

evidence.claim: 1556 corrected new edition of L'Huillier's missal; L'Huillier missal printed 1492.

stages.limitations: Corrections not specified; original not viewed.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1642 Meaux missal (Dominique Séguier)
stages.date_label: Missal dated 1642 (Allou)
stages.scope: Existence and date of Séguier's missal; its Roman orientation is inferred.
stages.witness_label: Missale Meldense, 1642 (Séguier)
stages.summary: Allou says that Séguier printed several liturgical books, that his 1640 breviary preface announced harmonising the Meaux liturgy with that of the universal Church, and that the missal is dated 1642. A catalogue record gives the missal's title as 'ad formam sacrosancti concilii Tridentini restitutum'.

evidence.claim: Séguier's books; 1640 breviary preface on harmony with the universal Church; missal dated 1642.

stages.limitations: Provisional: applying the breviary's stated Roman harmonisation to the missal is an inference supported only by a catalogue title. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1709 Meaux missal (Henri de Thiard de Bissy)
stages.date_label: Published 1709 (Allou)
stages.scope: Bissy's missal, prepared under Bossuet, as recorded.
stages.witness_label: Missale Meldense, 1709 (Bissy)
stages.summary: Allou says that Bishop Henri de Thiard de Bissy reprinted all the Meaux liturgical books. The missal, already worked on in Bossuet's time, appeared in 1709. The 1713 breviary followed, with many changes and a psalter distribution different from the Roman.

evidence.claim: Missal prepared under Bossuet, published 1709; 1713 breviary differing from the Roman.

stages.limitations: Allou's explicit non-Roman remark concerns the 1713 breviary; the missal's contents are not described. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1836 Meaux missal (Pruneau, under Gallard)
stages.date_label: Missal appeared 1836 (Allou); breviary 1834
stages.scope: The missal of Gallard's new diocesan liturgy, as recorded.
stages.witness_label: Missale Meldense, 1836
stages.summary: Allou says that because the Meaux books were running out, the Paris breviary and missal were adopted provisionally for the cathedral in 1824. Bishop Gallard then gave the diocese a new liturgy, with breviary offices following Paris and the rest by Canon Pruneau. The breviary appeared in 1834 and Pruneau's missal in 1836. The 1849 survey confirms the 1834 Pruneau liturgy and lists Meaux as having its own liturgy.

evidence.claim: 1824 provisional Paris books for the cathedral; Gallard's new liturgy; breviary 1834, Pruneau's missal 1836.
1834 Pruneau liturgy; table entry 'de Meaux'.

stages.limitations: Contents not described; the 1845 reissue was not found. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: Noyon missal of Charles de Broglie (attested by 1774)
stages.date_label: Attested by derivative books of 1774 and 1777; no printing year given
stages.scope: Existence of a Broglie missal, attested by its recorded title and by lay books that follow it.
stages.witness_label: Missale Noviomense (Charles de Broglie)
stages.summary: The Bibliographie noyonnaise records the title of a Missale Noviomense issued by Bishop Charles de Broglie's authority with chapter consent, known through a 1780 chapter memoir. It lists a 1774 Eucologe and 1777 Heures for Noyon that follow Bourzac's breviary and 'the missal printed by order of Mgr de Broglie'.

evidence.claim: Broglie missal title; Eucologe 1774 and Heures 1777 following Bourzac's breviary and Broglie's missal.

stages.limitations: Provisional: no copy, printing year or contents described. The Amiet-table year 1770 is not confirmed here.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1785 Sisteron missal (Suffren; Toulouse liturgy)
stages.date_label: Missale Sistaricense, Toulouse, Joseph Dalles, 1785 (cited imprint)
stages.scope: Existence, imprint and liturgical identity of the 1785 Sisteron missal as stated by Albanès.
stages.witness_label: Missale Sistaricense, Toulouse, Joseph Dalles, 1785
stages.summary: Albanès says Bishop Suffren introduced a new liturgy that had nothing of Sisteron but the name, being the Toulouse liturgy, even down to a proper preface for St Saturninus. Everything was printed at Toulouse: the breviary in 1778 and the missal seven years later, in 1785. His footnote cites the imprint: Missale Sistaricense, Toulouse, Joseph Dalles, 1785, quarto.

evidence.claim: Toulouse liturgy introduced under Suffren; breviary 1778; Missale Sistaricense, Toulouse, J. Dalles, 1785, in-4.

stages.limitations: The identification with the Toulouse liturgy is the historian's, citing contemporary opinion; no collation with the 1774 Toulouse missal. Original not viewed.
stages.reception: Not established.

stages.label: 1779 Montauban breviary-and-missal mandement
stages.date_label: Mandement dated 24 February 1779; obligatory from 28 November 1779 (Daux)
stages.scope: A mandated change of missal stated by Daux; no edition identified.
stages.witness_label: No exact edition identified
stages.summary: Daux reports a mandement of 24 February 1779 ordering in all churches the new breviary and missal of Montauban, with gradual and vesperal. The bishop says he chose, for uniformity with the metropolis, the breviary and missal already adopted by the other Toulouse suffragans, and their use became obligatory from 28 November 1779. Daux says the diocese was the last in France to take it.

evidence.claim: Mandement of 24 February 1779 ordering the new breviary and missal; obligatory from 28 November 1779.

stages.limitations: Provisional: no printed missal is identified. The catalogue's 1773 Missale Montalbanense and 1774 Missae pro defunctis predate this mandement, and the 1772 Nouvelles ecclésiastiques (cited in the 1849 survey) already lists Montauban among sees taking a Paris-type breviary. The conflict is unresolved.
stages.reception: Obligation from 28 November 1779 is stated; actual uptake not established.

stages.label: Rieux adoption of the Paris missal (reported 1778)
stages.date_label: Reported in the Nouvelles ecclésiastiques of 6 March 1778 as done 'some time ago'
stages.scope: A reported change from Roman to Paris breviary and missal; no edition identified.
stages.witness_label: No exact edition identified
stages.summary: The Nouvelles ecclésiastiques of 6 March 1778 report that Bishop de Lastic of Rieux had some time earlier wished to adopt the Paris breviary and missal in place of the Roman books still in use in the diocese. The chapter consented and left him the choice of edition. He chose the latest, which included the office and Mass of the Sacred Heart, to the displeasure of the chapter and many parish priests.

evidence.locus: RA1-PA37 (issue date) and RA1-PA39 ('De Rieux en Languedoc')
evidence.claim: Adoption of the Paris breviary and missal in place of the Roman books; Sacred Heart office in the chosen edition.

stages.limitations: Provisional: a partisan periodical report; no Rieux missal is described. The catalogue's 1776 Missale Rivense may be the resulting book, but that link is not stated by the source.
stages.reception: The report records chapter and clergy dissatisfaction; uptake not established.

stages.label: 1827 Nîmes diocesan liturgy (Larèche)
stages.date_label: Change dated 1827 by the 1849 survey
stages.scope: A reported change from the Roman to a new diocesan liturgy; the missal is not described.
stages.witness_label: No exact edition identified
stages.summary: The 1849 survey says that in 1827 Nîmes left the Roman for an entirely new liturgy composed by the abbé Larèche, vicar general of Bishop de Chaffoy; its table lists Nîmes as having its own liturgy. L'épiscopat français records that the diocesan synod of 27–29 September 1851 decreed the replacement of the Nîmes liturgy by the Roman.

evidence.claim: Nîmes left the Roman in 1827 for Larèche's new liturgy; table entry 'de Nîmes'.
Synod of 27–29 September 1851 decreed the replacement of the Nîmes liturgy by the Roman.

stages.limitations: Provisional: no missal is described; the catalogue's 1831 Missale Nemausense probably belongs to this liturgy, but no source viewed says so.
stages.reception: Not established.
